title: FINE, I guess this is how I’m pronouncing Godot now #waitingforgodot ...
transcript: another season another Jamie Lloyd show let's go and we're inside waiting for something but I don't know how to pronounce it Theatre of the absurd and Jamie Lloyd productions are often hit or miss for me so I was very hesitant going into this and you know what it was a pleasant surprise I thoroughly enjoyed waiting for Godot not gonna lie waiting for godot is the quintessential theatre of the absurd about two guys who are waiting for godot and that's it that's kind of the premise of the play uh occasionally other characters will come in and interact with them but the entire play is them passing the time waiting for this guy to show up the premise alone sounds painfully boring and yet with the writing of Samuel Beckett combined with this direction by Jamie Lloyd it it was thoroughly entertaining and I do think some of that is just how relatable I found the play with where I'm currently at in my life and how we sort of live in this really absurd reality uh where we are constantly waiting for the next thing whether that's you know the next show or the next horrible piece of news to drop so there is something so insanely relatable about these two guys who feel almost immobilised because of this one thing that they have to do uh and especially as somebody with adhd incredibly relatable but not only that I thought the direction and especially the visuals and the overall design of the show often times Jamie Lloyd Productions get accused of being incredibly minimal but I think the design of them is always really well thought out in just very abstract ways and this production was no exception the scenic design alone by Soutra Gilmour was so incredibly striking that I wasn't excited about this production until I saw that first production still but I also think that Jamie Lloyd does a really great job of not only using celebrity to enhance the text of whatever show he's directing uh and he does that incredibly well here with Keanu Reeves and Alex Winter who we already know from the Bill and Ted series have great chemistry with each other and we really get to see that on stage but he also does a great job of taking these scenes that could be so incredibly one note and repetitive and escalating them just enough as the play goes on to keep the audience engaged I was not bored for a single second in this play and I easily could have been I also love that in every Jamie Lloyd production you always have the celebrity names right that are not only really well chosen for the text that he's directing but also bring in the ticket sales but then he combines them with like some of the greatest theatrical performances you've ever seen on the stage and in this production you have Brandon J Dirden who I previously saw in Skeleton Crew and was incredible in that uh in this as Patso and then you have Michael Patrick Thornton who is previously in a Doll's House as lucky and they were both just so captivating and again I thought Alex Winter and Keanu Reeves definitely played so well against each other and Alex Winter is so comfortable on a stage I would love to see him do more theatre and then of course Keanu Reeves is Keanu Reeves his acting is not for everyone and it's a little bit stilted uh but when he's in the right role he really gets to shine and honestly he he worked for me he worked for me but I do not think that this show is going to be for everyone and the theatre of the absurd is kind of a very polarizing subgenre of theatre I do not think if you don't like Samuel Beckett plays or if you don't like absurdist theatre this isn't gonna win you over in the same way that despite the fact that I appreciated Jamie Lloyd's choices in a Doll's House that didn't win me over for that play as a whole but if you've never seen theatre of the absurd I think this is a pretty easily digestible foray into that type of theatre because ultimately even if the play doesn't resonate with you I think that the way that it's directed
